body:
(Replaces my note of 10:43 UTC, whose "trap" was wrong for the name. Corrected after reading server/.../library.py.)

WHERE: `applyPlaylists` (app/lib/data/encore/encore_writer.dart:153-215) writes the server's name, cover and `deletedAtMs: null` for every playlist row of the feed, then replaces entries and calls `_renumber`. The existing protection, `pendingStarTargets` (data/sync/pending_intent.dart:13), covers outbox kinds `star`/`unstar` only. Playlist kinds (outbox.dart:32-40): `playlist.create`, `playlist.update` (`playlistId`, `name?`, `add[]`, `removeIdx[]`, `removeIds[]`), `playlist.delete` (`id`).

WHAT THE SERVER DOES (library.py): a delivered rename, cover change or delete touches the PLAYLIST in the change log (lines 138, 147, 158), and `changes()` (363-405) returns the playlist row whole. So for name, cover and delete, skipping the write while an edit waits is safe: the delivery itself brings the playlist back in the next pull. Entries are different: `changes()` returns only the ENTRIES that were touched (one `entry` target each, 398-405), and the other device's entry has its own, older sequence number. Skipping it loses it for good. So protect per field, not per playlist:
 1. Name and cover: skip while a pending `playlist.update` carries `name`/`comment`. Keep CF-21: a playlist DELETED on the server wins over a waiting edit (docs/34), so the tombstone branch still applies.
 2. Entries: always apply the server's entries (they are idempotent by entry id), but (a) do not re-insert an entry whose track the phone removed and whose removal waits (`removeIds` of a pending update; removals are matched by track id, outbox.dart:34-36), and (b) do not delete the phone's own waiting adds. Those are rows with no entry id (`PlaylistEntriesCompanion.insert` without `entryId`, sync/playlist_mutations.dart:122-132), and `_renumber` (encore_writer.dart:225-232) deletes every row with a null entry id whenever a pull touches the playlist. That is a third way the screen undoes a waiting edit (read, not run): an added song vanishes until it is delivered. Keep null-id rows while an `add` for that playlist waits in the outbox.
 A parked (failed) edit stops protecting, as for likes (pending_intent.dart:5-8).

No new app call is needed. The end-to-end test is the arbiter: a rename waits, the feed brings the old name and another device's added song; the screen keeps the new name AND shows the song; after delivery both are there. Plus: an add waits, a pull touches the playlist, the added song stays; a removal waits, the feed brings the entry, it stays gone.

TESTS: encore_sync_test.dart:214 is the likes test (outbox insert at 221 is the pattern). Docs: docs/34 rule 5 (line 17) says "a like or unlike": widen it and its test column.
